tasks.task: Establish site and coordinate with occupants
tasks.scope: Site induction, occupied-building interface plan, emergency contact protocol, resident communication schedule, establish site office and waste management area in courtyard.
hazards: Tripping or slip on uneven courtyard surface during site setup
Struck by moving vehicle or plant during access to courtyard
Communication failure with occupants leading to uncontrolled entry into work zone
Heat stress or weather exposure during prolonged outdoor induction
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck by moving vehicle or plant during access to courtyard
controls: Brief all workers on occupied-building rules: no unannounced entry to common areas, no noise before 8 am or after 5 pm weekdays, no work Sundays.
Post site induction completion sign-off sheet at site office — do not allow any worker on site until inducted and signed.
Establish clear courtyard access route — mark with high-visibility tape, remove trip hazards, repair uneven surfaces before plant enters.
Appoint one site contact and provide occupants with phone number — confirm contact method, response time, and emergency escalation path.
Post resident communication schedule at main building entrance and site office — list work days, hours, and contact details for noise or access issues.
Conduct walk-through with building manager before first plant entry — confirm vehicle route, turning circles, overhead clearances, and no-go zones.
Install vehicle exclusion signs at courtyard entry if no plant is operating that day — remove before plant access resumes.
Establish waste management area in courtyard away from resident pathways — contain waste, prevent spillage, remove weekly.
Notify building occupants / body corporate / strata manager of work schedule, access restrictions, and expected noise/dust at least 48 hours before work starts
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow workers on site until: all inductees have completed White Card induction, signed attendance sheet, and reviewed occupied-building rules with site induction officer.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: unannounced occupant or visitor enters work zone and cannot be safely removed — stop plant, isolate area, brief occupant on hazards, resume only when occupant has left.
🛑 STOP WORK if: courtyard access route becomes blocked or uneven surface creates trip hazard — repair before resuming plant movement or pedestrian access.
🛑 STOP WORK if: resident communication log shows two or more complaints within one shift — review method with building manager and site contact before resuming.
admin: Retain signed site induction attendance sheet — verify all workers and visitors are inducted before access.
Maintain resident communication log — record date, time, issue, resolution, and occupant contact name.
Conduct pre-start meeting with building manager and site supervisor — confirm access route, emergency protocols, and occupant notification method.
Issue occupied-building site rules poster to all workers — cover noise curfews, access restrictions, emergency contacts.
Establish site office location and confirm utilities (power, phone, water) are available.
Confirm waste contractor collection schedule — schedule pickups to avoid occupant disturbance or blocked common areas.
Residents responsible for clearing personal items, furniture, potted plants, and non-common fixtures from balcony and work areas before each phase — area left/excluded if not cleared
Temporary access to neighbouring properties required — confirm access arrangements before commencing
Vegetation trimmed away from surfaces designated for painting or remedial works prior to commencement — area excluded if vegetation impedes access
On-site parking or provision of parking permits required for duration of works
Final inspection and agreed scope of works to be confirmed before commencement
ppe: High-visibility vest (Class D) during courtyard access and setup.
Hard hat when working under or near overhead structures (if scaffolding present).

monitoring.critical_control: Exclusion zone barriers complete, signage visible, access controlled
monitoring.evidence: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry
monitoring.what_to_look_for: Barriers intact, signage legible, no unauthorised entry

responsibility.SUP: Verify exclusion zone complete, barriers intact, access controlled before work starts
responsibility.WKR: Set up and maintain barriers, stop work if zone breached, report access issues

tasks.task: Erect scaffold access via Kiora Lane and courtyard
tasks.scope: Install temporary scaffold over 4m to balconies per engineer design, secure anchor points, install edge protection and working platforms, final inspection before handover to works teams.
hazards: Fall from height during scaffold erection — working at 4m+ without fall arrest
Scaffold collapse or failure — anchor points inadequate or insufficiently tested
Struck by falling tools, materials or scaffold components during assembly
Manual handling injury during transport and positioning of scaffold frames and braces
Loss of edge protection during installation — unprotected gaps during phase assembly
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during scaffold erection — working at 4m+ without fall arrest
controls: Obtain signed scaffold erection permit from licenced scaffolder before any component installation.
Verify engineer design drawings and load calculations match site anchor points and building structure.
Install temporary edge protection and safety barriers around Kiora Lane access before personnel enter.
Secure all anchor points to structural elements using bolts or chemical anchors certified for load.
Install working platforms, cross-braces and guard rails per engineer design before any worker access.
Conduct load test of completed scaffold structure — verify no deflection or movement under test load.
Tag scaffold with unique identifier and inspection date upon final completion.
Brief all workers on scaffold assembly sequence, anchor locations, and prohibited zones before work starts.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not allow worker access to scaffold until: handover certificate issued by licenced scaffolder and site supervisor signed off.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not proceed to next phase until: anchor points load-tested and documented by competent person.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any scaffold component shows damage, rust, or deformation during assembly.
🛑 STOP WORK if: anchor point or building structural element shows crack, separation or weakness.
🛑 STOP WORK if: environmental conditions (wind >40 km/h, rain, lightning risk) prevent safe assembly.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: tell building occupants and public of scaffold work — post warning signage on Kiora Lane and courtyard access.
Restrict access to scaffold work zone — barricade courtyard perimeter and establish exclusion zone below platform.
Record anchor point testing results and load certification — retain on site throughout scaffold life.
Conduct pre-use inspection each shift — document scaffold condition on site log.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Full-body harness with shock absorber lanyard (when working above 2m during assembly)

monitoring.critical_control: Verify anchor points are secured and load-tested before platform installation.
monitoring.evidence: Load test certificate, anchor point inspection photos, scaffolder sign-off on permit

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

tasks.task: Remove existing membrane, screed and tile bed
tasks.scope: Strip tile bed, screed and waterproofing membrane from balcony surfaces. Dust control and silica management during removal. Collect and segregate waste. Leave slab substrate exposed for crack investigation.
hazards: Inhalation of silica dust during tile cutting and removal — no wet suppression applied
Silica overexposure causing long-term respiratory harm
Cut or laceration to hands and fingers during tile and membrane stripping
Trip or fall on debris-laden scaffold platform
Struck by falling tiles or debris from height onto occupants or public below
tasks.dominant_hazard: Struck by falling tiles or debris from height onto occupants or public below
controls: Wet all tile surfaces with water spray before cutting or breaking to suppress silica dust generation.
Use dust extraction shroud or local exhaust ventilation on power tools during tile removal and concrete exposure.
Fit workers with P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted and tested before starting work; change filter each shift or when resistance increases.
Barricade balcony perimeter with heavy-duty debris netting secured to scaffold to catch falling tiles and prevent ejection to public below.
Manually strip membrane using hand tools only; do not use power tools on membrane to avoid aerosol generation.
Separate tiles, screed, and membrane waste into labelled bins on scaffold platform; do not drop waste over edge.
Wear cut-resistant gloves and hi-viz shirt or vest
Sweep and vacuum exposed slab with HEPA filter vacuum after each section removed; do not dry sweep.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start tile removal until: debris netting is fully installed and tensioned around balcony perimeter.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not expose slab substrate until: all silica suppression equipment (water pump, extraction, RPE) is tested and operational.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: debris netting tears or separates from scaffold during removal; repair or replace before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker RPE filter becomes wet, damaged, or fit fails; replace and refit before re-entry.
🛑 STOP WORK if: water suppression pump fails or is not maintaining wet surfaces on active removal area.
admin: Obtain and display Scaffold Erection Permit signed by licensed scaffolder before any worker access.
Obtain Scaffold Handover Certificate from scaffolder; verify on site before commencement.
Obtain Working at Heights Permit signed by site supervisor; display on scaffold.
Obtain Environmental Protection Authority (EPA) waste removal licence; provide to waste contractor.
Prepare Noise Management Plan; tell occupants of work schedule and times.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) before induction.
Verify Scaffolding Licence class matches scaffold type and height; copy on file.
Verify Working at Heights competency (RIIOHS204E or current equivalent) for all elevated workers.
Obtain and brief all workers on membrane product Safety Data Sheet; store on site.
Conduct daily toolbox talk on silica hazard, fall prevention, and public exclusion protocol.
ppe: P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) fitted and tested before each use; refit and filter change each shift.
Hard hat with chin strap when working on open scaffold.

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during removal; check before each new section started.
monitoring.evidence: Visual observation of wet tile surface; dust extraction fan noise audible; worker RPE log signed daily with filter condition noted; debris netting visual inspection record (daily).

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Remove existing membrane, screed and
responsibility.WKR: Perform Remove existing membrane, screed and per SWMS

tasks.scope: check exposed slab substrate for cracks, spalling and structural defects. Mark all defects. Leo and Associates inspection and hold point before repair work proceeds. Document findings and obtain written approval to continue.
hazards: Fall from height — worker slips on exposed slab during inspection at 4m+
Struck by falling tools or inspection equipment during detailed examination
Contact with spalling edges — sharp concrete debris during marking
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker slips on exposed slab during inspection at 4m+
controls: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licensed scaffolder and retained on site before any worker accesses platform.
Verify scaffold tag current and visible at platform entry — do not work if tag expired or missing.
Check slab surface for wet, algae, loose debris, or spalling before starting inspection — defer work if surface conditions create slip risk.
Wear fall arrest harness rated for suspension and connect lanyard to certified anchor point before stepping onto slab.
Walk slowly across slab — test footing with each step and stop immediately if surface feels unstable or wet.
Mark all cracks, spalls, and structural defects with chalk or tape — photograph marked defects for Leo and Associates review.
Bag all loose spalling concrete fragments into disposal container — do not handle sharp edges bare-handed.
Wear cut-resistant gloves when touching spalled edges or marking concrete surfaces.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit worker onto slab until: scaffold handover certificate is signed, tag is current, and harness/lanyard are fitted and anchor point confirmed.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: slab surface becomes wet, algae-covered, or covered in loose debris making safe footing impossible.
🛑 STOP WORK if: worker reports foot slip, loss of balance, or harness malfunction — evacuate immediately and recheck anchor and surface condition.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Leo and Associates inspection is incomplete or written approval to proceed with repair has not been received.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Retain scaffold erection permit, handover certificate, and working at heights permit on site — accessible to all workers.
Schedule Leo and Associates inspection before any repair work is planned — confirm inspection date with PM and resident.
Document all marked defects photographically — store images with inspection report for approval trail.
Record worker names, times of inspection, weather conditions, and any surface slip incidents in site log.
tell residents 24 hours before inspection to manage access and make sure occupied areas are not disrupted.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Fall arrest harness (AS/NZS 1891.1 rated, regularly tested)
Lanyard with shock absorber (max 2 m, rated 1.5 kN minimum)
Hard hat (standard construction, compliant with AS/NZS 1801)

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each shift start and after any surface condition change
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of harness fit, anchor point certification tag, lanyard connection — record worker name and time in site log; photograph anchor setup if non-standard.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.task: Repair slab substrate cracks and spalling
tasks.scope: Repair identified cracks and spalling using approved epoxy or concrete repair material. Clean and prepare surfaces. Cure per manufacturer specification before membrane application.
hazards: Inhalation of epoxy vapour or concrete dust during preparation and application
Skin or eye contact with epoxy resin — chemical burn
Slip on wet or cured material on scaffold platform at height
Manual handling injury during surface preparation — grinding, chipping, high-force tools
tasks.dominant_hazard: Slip on wet or cured material on scaffold platform at height
controls: Review SDS for epoxy or repair material before starting — check ventilation requirements and cure time.
Wet-grind or chip substrate using water suppression — do not create dry dust during surface prep.
Apply epoxy or repair material per manufacturer instructions — match temperature, humidity, and cure time.
Prevent slips on scaffold platform — cover cured or wet material with anti-slip matting or remove wet residue daily.
Keep epoxy resin in secondary containment and away from edge — prevent spill onto occupied areas below.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection— change gloves if torn or wet.
make sure forced air ventilation on scaffold if epoxy vapour detected — position fan to clear work area.
Barricade scaffold platform edge with guard rail or netting — prevent dropped tools or material hitting occupants below.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane or proceed to next phase until: substrate cured per SDS, surface dry, and slip hazard removed from platform.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: worker slips or near-slip on wet material on scaffold platform — review and reapply slip controls.
🛑 STOP WORK if: epoxy vapour visible and ventilation fan not operating — restart fan and clear platform.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold platform guard rail removed or damaged — repair or reinstate before continuing.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker access.
Obtain working at heights permit signed by supervisor before each elevated repair task.
Brief all workers on SDS for epoxy or concrete repair material — cover hazards, first aid, spill response.
Confirm manufacturer cure time — record on daily work log and site board to prevent premature covering.
Establish noise management protocol if grinding disturbs occupants — use water suppression to reduce noise and dust.
check scaffold platform daily for wet residue, cured material buildup, or slip hazards — remove or cover before shift starts.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Hard hat with chin strap (fall from height).
Respiratory protection — P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) minimum if dust generated without water suppression; organic vapour cartridge if epoxy fumes detected.
High-visibility vest (occupied building, working above occupied areas).
Hearing protection if grinding exceeds 85 dB (manage per noise plan).

monitoring.critical_control: Dust extraction running and P2 respirator fitted before each grinding cycle
monitoring.frequency: Each shift start and after any epoxy application or rain.
monitoring.evidence: Daily site inspection record — photograph of platform condition, note slip hazards addressed, record matting installed or residue removed.

responsibility.SUP: Supervise repairs, check scaffold safety, approve debris controls, sign hold points
responsibility.WKR: Perform repairs per SWMS, wear PPE, use dust control, report defects

tasks.scope: Prime and seal prepared substrate. Apply new waterproofing membrane per manufacturer specification and design drawing. Install membrane to all balcony surfaces, upturns and penetrations. Cure and conduct water test hold point before screed application.
hazards: Inhalation of primer or membrane fumes — poor ventilation at height, enclosed balconies
Skin or eye contact with primer or membrane during application
Slip on wet membrane or primer on exposed slab at 4m+
Heat stress or respiratory irritation in high-temperature cure conditions
Fall during water-test stage — wet and slippery platform surfaces
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall during water-test stage — wet and slippery platform surfaces
controls: Obtain SDS for primer and membrane product before work starts.
Ventilate balcony continuously during primer application using portable fan directed away from workers and building interior.
Apply primer and membrane in thin, even coats per manufacturer specification to control fume release and cure time.
Wear chemical-resistant gloves and eye protection
Establish slip control on wet membrane surface by placing anti-slip tape or grit strips on walkways and work platforms.
Barricade wet membrane area with hazard tape and signs — restrict access until cured per manufacturer cure schedule.
Conduct water test only after full cure completion — verify cure time in writing before water application.
make sure water test platform remains dry between test cycles — mop and air dry between test stages to prevent slip hazard build-up.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not apply membrane until: primer has fully cured per SDS and substrate is visually dry
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not conduct water test until: membrane has cured for full period specified in manufacturer technical data sheet, confirmed in writing by supervisor
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: fume levels cause respiratory irritation or dizziness in any worker — evacuate and increase ventilation before restart
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker slips on wet membrane or primer during application or water-test stage — stop all work until slip hazard is eliminated
🛑 STOP WORK if: cure time cannot be verified in writing from manufacturer data sheet before water test commences
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Verify scaffold erection permit and handover certificate signed by licensed scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Verify working-at-heights permit completed and signed before elevated task starts.
Confirm all workers hold current White Card and working-at-heights competency verification.
Confirm SDS training completion for primer and membrane product — record attendance.
Record primer application start time and temperature — cross-check against manufacturer minimum cure-temperature requirement.
Record full membrane cure completion date and time in site diary before water-test authorisation.
tell building management of water-test schedule and any noise or fume release — obtain occupant consent if required.
Brief occupants of occupied building on restricted access to balcony during cure and water-test phases.
ppe: eye protection— required during primer and membrane application
Respirator with organic vapour cartridge if fume levels persist despite ventilation — fit-test certificate required
Non-slip steel-capped footwear— compulsory during water-test phase
High-visibility vest — required for work at height on occupied building

monitoring.critical_control: Ventilation operating and fume concentration below manufacturer threshold during primer application — verified by smell test and worker symptom check.
monitoring.frequency: Continuous during primer and membrane application; each water-test cycle before worker entry
monitoring.evidence: Portable fan running throughout application; supervisor notes on absence of fume odour or respiratory irritation; cure-time record signed by supervisor; photograph of anti-slip tape placement on wet platform

responsibility.SUP: Supervise Apply new waterproofing membrane system
responsibility.WKR: Perform Apply new waterproofing membrane system per SWMS

tasks.scope: Install reinforced screed to final fall. Tile bed and tiles to balcony surfaces. Reinstate balustrades, skirting and edge trim per original detail or engineer drawing. Grout and seal joints. Cure fully before occupation.
hazards: Fall from height — worker loses balance on wet screed or during tile installation at 4m+
Struck by falling tiles, tools or materials onto occupants or public below
Manual handling injury — repeated bending, lifting of screed bags and tiles
Cut or laceration during tile cutting on scaffold platform
Silica dust inhalation during tile cutting and grouting
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height — worker loses balance on wet screed or during tile installation at 4m+
controls: Confirm scaffold handover certificate signed by licenced scaffolder before any worker accesses platform.
Install edge protection and fall arrest points on scaffold platform per engineer drawing before screed delivery.
Wet screed surface immediately after laying to prevent dust and reduce slip hazard during finishing.
Establish exclusion zone below balcony work — barricade and delineate on ground 6 m minimum radius.
Cut tiles on designated bench below platform level — not on scaffold platform.
Use dust extraction or damp suppression at tile cut point — no dry cutting on platform.
Remove loose debris and tile offcuts from platform edge and scaffold frame daily before close-out.
Restrict access to wet screed and tile bed — place 'wet surface' signs at platform access points.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not install tiles until: screed has cured per membrane manufacturer specification and is confirmed dry by site supervisor.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not permit public or occupants below work area until: exclusion zone fencing is in place and edge protection is certified.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: wind speed exceeds 40 km/h or visibility below 50 m — platform becomes unstable or tools/materials become flight risk.
🛑 STOP WORK if: scaffold handover certificate cannot be produced or any section shows visible damage, rust or missing components.
🛑 STOP WORK if: harness, lanyard or anchor point is damaged, shows wear or is not independently verified as compliant.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display working at heights permit signed by supervisor before platform access.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) and working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent).
Review SDS for screed membrane and tile adhesive — communicate hazards and ventilation needs at toolbox meeting.
Appoint site supervisor to monitor exclusion zone and stop work if occupants or public breach barricade.
Record daily platform safety checks — document edge protection, harness condition, debris removal, anchor points.
ppe: Safety harness and shock-absorbing lanyard — correctly worn and clipped to certified anchor point always.
Hard hat — no exceptions on platform or below exclusion zone.
Steel-capped boots with slip-resistant sole — required on wet screed and tile bed surfaces.
P2 mask/respirator (fit-tested) — required for tile cutting and dry grouting work (if dust extraction fails).
High-visibility vest — all workers on platform and spotters in exclusion zone.

monitoring.critical_control: Verify harness is clipped to anchor point before worker enters platform — visually confirm clip engagement.
monitoring.frequency: Before each worker accesses platform — continuous observation during work.
monitoring.evidence: Daily checklist: harness condition, anchor point certification, exclusion zone integrity, edge protection visual check, handover certificate on site.

responsibility.SUP: Verify fall protection, check module weights, sign off hold points
responsibility.WKR: Wear fall harness, check lanyard attachment, report equipment damage

tasks.scope: Leo and Associates final inspection of completed works. fix identified defects. Conduct water test to verify membrane and seal integrity. Obtain final sign-off before demobilisation.
hazards: Fall from height during final inspection — working on exposed balcony at 4m+ with edge protection removed or incomplete
Slips and trips on wet test water or remaining wet surfaces
Struck by falling tools or materials during remedial work
Trip hazard from temporary protective measures or test apparatus
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during final inspection — working on exposed balcony at 4m+ with edge protection removed or incomplete
controls: Verify scaffold handover certificate is signed and posted before any worker accesses the platform.
Check all edge protection (guardrails, mid-rails, toe-boards) is installed and secure before starting inspection.
Confirm working at heights permit is signed and current before each elevated task begins.
Barricade all wet test areas with hazard tape and warning signs to prevent slip entry.
Identify and secure or remove all trip hazards from test apparatus, hoses, and temporary protective measures.
Brief all workers on defect locations, remedial sequence, and fall arrest points before work starts.
check all harness attachment points and anchor lines for damage before harness use.
Stop all remedial work if edge protection is incomplete, removed, or damaged during the task.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start final inspection until: scaffold handover certificate is signed by licenced scaffolder and all edge protection is installed and checked.
⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not conduct water test until: all temporary protective measures are secured and barricaded, and occupants are notified and protected from wet surfaces.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: any edge protection is missing, damaged, or removed during the task.
🛑 STOP WORK if: wet test water creates slip hazard that cannot be controlled or drained within 15 minutes.
🛑 STOP WORK if: any worker works at height without current working at heights permit or harness inspection.
🛑 STOP WORK if: occupant balcony below work zone is not closed and barricaded
admin: Obtain and display scaffold erection permit signed by licenced scaffolder before scaffold is used.
Obtain scaffold handover certificate from scaffolder before any worker accesses the platform.
Obtain and display working at heights permit signed by supervisor before each elevated task.
Verify all workers hold current White Card (CPCCWHS1001) or equivalent site induction.
Verify all workers hold current scaffolding licence (class appropriate to scaffold type and height).
Verify all workers hold current working at heights competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent per RII Training Package).
tell all building occupants before water test begins; provide 24-hour notice if test may affect occupied spaces.
Record final inspection findings and remedial work completed; document sign-off from Leo and Associates before demobilisation.
Close and barricade balconies directly below active work zone before elevated work starts each day
Notify affected residents before any noise/dust generating work on their level or adjacent levels
ppe: Safety harness and lanyard (tested and tagged, attached to certified anchor point during all work at height over 2m).
Hard hat with chin strap (occupied building — falling tool risk).

monitoring.critical_control: Defect list reviewed and signed off by supervisor before rectification starts
monitoring.frequency: before each elevated task and continuously during work
monitoring.evidence: Visual check of guardrails, mid-rails, toe-boards; handover certificate on-site; working at heights permit signed and displayed.

responsibility.SUP: Verify access equipment safe, approve defect list, sign off completion
responsibility.WKR: Inspect per specification, photograph defects, report issues

tasks.scope: Dismantle and remove all temporary scaffold from courtyard and Kiora Lane. Make good courtyard surface, remove site office and waste containment. Final clean-up and site handover to building manager.
hazards: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling — working unsupported at 4m+ during removal phases
Struck by falling scaffold components during removal
Manual handling injury during transport of scaffold frames and components
Loss of access integrity mid-dismantling — unprotected fall hazard as platform shrinks
tasks.dominant_hazard: Fall from height during scaffold dismantling — working unsupported at 4m+ during removal phases
controls: Stop all dismantling work if wind speed exceeds 10 m/s or gusts exceed 15 m/s — check hourly with anemometer.
Erect exclusion zone 2 m radius around base of scaffold — barricade with tape and signs, prohibit all public and worker access.
Work only from within scaffold platform or harness-secured to scaffold structure — no standing on frame edges or cross-bracing.
Lower all loose components hand-to-hand into bin at ground level — do not drop or throw components.
Dismantle platform sections top-to-bottom, removing handrails and guard rails first, then decking, then standards — secure remaining structure after each stage.
Wear full body harness lanyard-connected to independent scaffold fall arrest point before stepping off final platform.
Brief all workers on dismantling sequence and exclusion zone before starting work each day.
Conduct tool-box talk identifying which component removal stage is in progress and which workers are at height.
hold_points: ⚠️ HOLD POINT — do not start dismantling until: Licensed scaffolder confirms on-site and all workers briefed on removal sequence and exclusion zone.
stop_work: 🛑 STOP WORK if: Wind gusts exceed 15 m/s or any visible movement or sway is detected in remaining scaffold structure.
🛑 STOP WORK if: Any public or unauthorised person enters 2 m exclusion zone during dismantling.
🛑 STOP WORK if: More than one worker is at height simultaneously without independent fall arrest points or harness check is incomplete.
admin: Obtain written confirmation from licensed scaffolder that scaffold is safe to dismantle before work starts.
Verify scaffold dismantling permit is signed and current before first worker enters exclusion zone.
Record daily wind speed checks and dismantling stage progress in site logbook.
Conduct pre-start toolbox talk naming responsible workers, exclusion zone boundaries, and current dismantling stage.
Photograph or video record exclusion zone signage and barrier setup before dismantling begins.
Keep anemometer on site and check wind speed hourly — record results in site diary.
ppe: Full body harness (when at height or on final platform sections)

monitoring.critical_control: Confirm harness is clipped to independent fall arrest point before each worker steps onto platform or frame.
monitoring.frequency: continuous during dismantling, checked before each elevated work phase
monitoring.evidence: Visual confirmation of lanyard attachment point and secure anchor; worker name and time recorded in site logbook; daily photo of harness setup and exclusion zone.

responsibility.SUP: Verify scaffold or EWP certification, supervise erection, sign off load checks
responsibility.WKR: Follow erection plan, wear harness at height, report defects

inference.hrcw_category: WHS Reg 2017 Sch 3 cl.6 — Work on scaffold over 4m
inference.hrcw_license_class: Scaffolding Licence — Basic (SB), Intermediate (SI), or Advanced (SA)
ppe: Hard hat where overhead risk present
Full-body harness — when erecting or dismantling above 4m
Energy-absorbing lanyard — double lanyard where continuous attachment required
P2 half-face respirator — lead paint and possible asbestos dust
Disposable coveralls — taped at wrists and ankles
Full body harness with double lanyard — when working on incomplete scaffold
UV protection — long sleeves, sunscreen, wide-brim hat where harness permits
certifications: Scaffolding Licence — class appropriate to scaffold type and height
Working at heights — verified current competency (RIIOHS204E or equivalent per current RII Training Package)
SDS training — safety data sheet for membrane product
Licensed waterproofer — where AS 3740 compliance required
EWP operator licence — WP class where boom exceeds 11m
Hazardous materials survey — before removal of any old corrugated roof
Lead Assessor Class A — where lead paint confirmed or suspected
Asbestos inspection — where asbestos-backed insulation suspected
Scaffolding high risk work licence — Basic (modular, prefab, bracket, fall arrest)
permits: Scaffold erection permit — signed by licenced scaffolder before use
Handover certificate — before any worker uses completed scaffold
Working at heights permit — signed before each elevated task
Noise management plan — required where work affects occupants
Dust containment plan — hoarding or plastic sheeting before work starts
Owners corporation consent — special resolution required for common property works
Strata by-law compliance — check all applicable by-laws before work
Building manager approval — written consent before work in common areas
Hazmat removal plan — documented before old roof removal commences
Scaffold permit to strip — required before dismantling any scaffold from which a person or object could fall >4m
Roof access permit — before any worker accesses roof
qualifications: Competent person — weekly inspection and after adverse weather
Structural engineer — where scaffold exceeds 15m or non-standard loading
Applicator certification — manufacturer certification for warranty purposes
Rescue plan — documented before work above 2m begins
Rescue equipment — on site and ready for immediate deployment before any elevated work starts
Occupant notification — 48 hours minimum before noisy or dusty work
Exclusion zone — clearly marked, prevents public access to work area
